name: Rotator Cuff Repair Rehabilitation
summary: A staged programme protects the healing tendon first, then restores movement, strength and function; timing and loading follow the surgeon's protocol, which depends on the tear size and repair quality.

looksLike: Surgeon's protocol, tear size and repair type
Passive and active range as permitted
redFlags: Signs of infection (heat, redness, fever, wound leakage)
Sudden loss of active elevation or a pop with weakness (possible re-tear)
Hot, swollen calf or chest pain
New numbness or weakness in the arm

Teach sling and sleeping positions and hand, wrist and elbow movement.
Show the first permitted exercises and what to avoid.
selfCare: Avoid lifting and pushing with the operated arm until cleared
Gradual return to light daily use

stages.label: Treat: build capacity
stages.goal: Stiffness and weakness both limit recovery, so the programme balances protection with timely, graded movement.
when: Baseline recorded: Shoulder range of motion
do: Early elbow, wrist and hand movement
Pendulum and passive range in the early weeks
Progressive cuff and deltoid strengthening later
dose: Early passive range and pendulums: 3 to 4 times a day for 5 to 10 minutes.
Active-assisted range: 10 to 15 repetitions, 2 to 3 times a day when cleared.
Active range and scapular control: 2 to 3 sets of 10 repetitions when cleared.
Strengthening: 2 to 3 sets of 8 to 12 repetitions, starting light, usually after about 12 weeks.

Return to lifting, work and sport in graded steps
